Subject: Next steps: MSA/DPA owners, redline sequencing & turnaround

Hi Lisa / Matt — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment on owners and expected turn times.

Call recap (very short):
- Use case: Atlas wants Redwood to power clinical note summarization for pilot across 3 hospitals.
- Key concerns from your side: data residency, DPA language on processing/return/destruction, and procurement timing for PO.

Proposed legal/contract sequence and owners:
1) NDA — already executed, we have that on file.
2) MSA (commercial terms + liability) — Redwood legal will own initial redline and consolidated pass. Recommended owner at Redwood: Karthik Iyer (copied).
3) DPA — privacy team / legal at Atlas will want to review; we can run parallel redlines if that helps.
4) SOW — finalize scope & pricing; procurement issues (PO) typically come after SOW sign-off.

Turnaround guidance (Redwood-side):
- MSA: initial pass 1–2 business days, consolidated redline within 3 business days.
- DPA: we can provide a Prisma-style DPA template; expect 3–7 business days depending on privacy questions.
- SOW: iterative; depends on scope changes.

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_draft_v2.docx (recommended starting point), Atlas_SOW_v0.3.pdf, redline_guidelines.txt

Asks for Atlas:
- Please confirm the following owners: who on your side will own legal/MSA, who will own privacy/DPA, and who is the procurement PO contact.
- Would Atlas be open to parallel MSA + DPA redlines to shorten overall calendar time?

If agreed, Karthik will take the lead on the Redwood redline for the MSA and Marcus will coordinate SOW/pricing edits. Happy to set a short 30-min sync if helpful.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi all — Marcus from Solutions here, brief operational note from the Redwood side: 

1) Parallel redlines are fine and in many cases shorten calendar time. Our recommended sequencing is still: MSA -> DPA -> SOW, but we can accept parallel exchange of MSA + DPA redlines and work to consolidate simultaneously.

2) Typical internal turn times (Redwood):
- MSA: 2–3 business days for initial redline pass; if there are complex indemnity or insurance asks that can extend to 5 business days.
- DPA: 3–7 business days depending on legal/privacy questions and required edits to security appendices.
- SOW: we try to lock scope in 1–2 days after wording is agreed; pricing changes sometimes need product/finance review which can add time.

3) Procurement notes: if Atlas requires a PO before prod activation, we can accept a PO post-SOW signature. We'll surface the PO requirement up the chain to ensure billing/setup timelines are aligned.

Operational asks for Atlas: please share the Atlas legal alias and procurement PO contact (email). If you can provide a single point of contact for redline delivery that will make consolidation faster.

I'll also put together a short "redline playbook" (one-pager) and share it here for clarity.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
